problem: Existing adversarial attacks on VLN agents (texture changes, patches, universal perturbations) create unnatural textures that indoor agents rarely see, and they mostly need white-box access. Robustness to natural scene attributes such as lighting is largely unstudied.
motivation: Indoor lighting is intrinsic, common and easy to control, so failures under it matter in practice. A pilot study on SPOC ObjectNav (CHORES, 200 episodes, intensity 0 to 2 in steps of 0.1) shows irregular, non-monotonic success-rate fluctuations with a gap of about 10 points between best and worst intensity. This suggests deliberately chosen lighting could expose systematic vulnerabilities.
key_idea: A black-box attack that manipulates global indoor light: SILA searches one constant intensity per episode via a timestep-weighted trajectory loss, and DILA switches the light on or off at steps where a one-step lookahead predicts larger heading deviation from the goal.
insight: Lighting alone, without unusual textures, substantially breaks VLN agents, and time-varying switching is much stronger than static lighting (e.g., SPOC-ObjectNav ASR 60.38 to 96.23). Ablations show that the loss weighting matters modestly: the timestep-weighted loss beats the final-step and unweighted losses. Lookahead-guided switching beats random switching with the same switch count, and ASR rises with the number of switches allowed (unlimited is best), so attack strength comes from repeated well-timed abrupt changes.
method: Problem formulation: the attacker controls only a global light-intensity sequence L={l_1..l_T}; the observation is o_t=r(E,s_t,l_t), and the attack succeeds if the agent never issues STOP inside the goal region G.
SILA timestep-weighted loss: J = sum_t (t/T̂)·||pos(s_t)−G||_2, giving later steps larger weight because late errors are irreversible.

SILA black-box search: each iteration renders l±α (clipped to [lmin,lmax]), runs both episodes, and moves toward the intensity with the larger loss. An ε-greedy rule occasionally flips the direction, and the search stops early on failure. Default bounds are [0,1.5] and α=0.05.
DILA on/off switching: light is either l* (taken from SILA) or 0, so l_t=i_t·l*.

DILA one-step lookahead surrogate: at each step, simulate the action under the current and the switched lighting, compute the angle β between the toward-target vector and the heading, and switch if β_sw−β_cur>0. This avoids full rollouts and credit-assignment problems.
Query model: only the agent's position and heading are returned per black-box query.

setting.backbone: SPOC and FLaRe (official pretrained checkpoints, frozen; they are the victim models, and the attack itself is a gradient-free search)
setting.training_data: none for the attack (victim models used without fine-tuning; the attack is optimized per episode at test time)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB camera (victim model input); the attacker observes agent position and heading
setting.action_space: low-level discrete navigation actions in AI2-THOR (attacker action: light intensity / on-off switch)
setting.privileged: attacker uses the goal location G and per-query agent position/heading; the clean-success episode set is used for ASR

numbers.extra: black-box attack; ASR and EL are attack metrics, not navigation SR
numbers.evidence: Table 1 attack performance on SPOC and FLaRe over ObjectNav, Fetch, RoomVisit

numbers.extra: SILA alone already gives the same numbers

numbers_note: Metrics are attack success rate (ASR, over clean-success episodes) and episode length (EL), not navigation SR/SPL. The paper gives no clean SR. Test splits have 200/200/172 episodes. Only SPOC-ObjectNav SILA is listed as an extra variant, and the other SILA-only rows are in Table 1.
results: SILA+DILA reaches ASR of 52.73 to 100 across the two models and three tasks, beating Texture-GA (37.57 to 87.50) and Random Intensity. On SPOC-ObjectNav, ASR is 96.23 versus 54.90 for Texture-GA, and EL roughly doubles versus SILA (131.07 to 234.27). DILA adds 5.46 to 35.85 points over SILA except on SPOC-Fetch, which is already at 100.
limitations: Attacker assumes control of a single global light and access to agent position and heading per query, and it uses the goal location; this is a strong assumption.
Evaluated only in the AI2-THOR simulator on two models (SPOC, FLaRe) from one benchmark (CHORES), with no real-world lighting tests and no defenses.
Per-episode search needs many repeated rollouts (many queries).
builds_on: Texture-based physical adversarial attacks (Chen et al. 2024)
compares_to: Texture-GA (black-box variant of Chen et al. physicalizable attack)
